draft.headline: Jake White starts where Fiji lost a final
beats: Five weeks ago on this ground Japan beat Fiji 20–15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final. Fiji have since appointed Jake White, 62, the 2007 World Cup winner. His first game is the rematch.
White was chosen from 31 applicants, replacing interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula. He wants Fiji to play like Fiji, only with "a little bit more structure, a little bit more formation".
Form leans one way. Japan have won three straight, including 63–14 against USA and 57–12 against Canada. Fiji have won once in five tests this year, and conceded 73 to England in July.
Ninth meets tenth, and the loser has further to fall. A Fiji win puts them ninth. Whoever loses drops below Wales and Italy, 12th at best.
A fortnight later both are in Europe, Japan at Wales and Fiji at France.

draft.headline: White's first Fiji game is a rematch of September's final
beats: Five weeks ago on this ground Japan beat Fiji 20–15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final, their first title since 2019. Fiji's response was to hire Jake White, the 2007 World Cup winner, from 31 applicants. His first match is the same opponent at the same ground.
One place separates them, ninth and tenth. A Fiji win swaps that. A Japan win drops Fiji below Wales and Italy; a Japan defeat does the same to Japan.

Form favours the hosts: 57–12 over Canada, 63–14 over the USA, then the final. Fiji have won once in 2026, and lost 8–73 to England in July. White, 62, wants them to "play like Fiji but just give them a little bit more structure, a little bit more formation".
A fortnight on, both are in Europe for the Nations Championship: Japan at Wales, Fiji at France.

draft.headline: Any Pumas win takes Ireland's third place
beats: Ireland have been third in the world in every table since July. Any Argentina win in Dublin ends that and drops them below France. Win by 16 or more and the Pumas also climb above Australia into seventh.

Argentina's last win was 35–21 over Wales on 11 July. Since then they have lost 24–31 to England and 10–17 to South Africa, then lost 21–27 to Australia and drew 28–28 with them. Close, mostly. Not wins.

Ireland last played on 18 July, losing 21–40 to New Zealand after five straight wins. Andy Farrell is without captain Caelan Doris, still sidelined, and Jack Conan's shoulder needed further assessment before the squad was named.
The Championship table is tight. Ireland sit sixth, level on points with Scotland. Argentina are eighth, a point behind Australia.
Next for Ireland it is Fiji at home, with the Springboks in town on 21 November. Argentina go to Italy.

draft.headline: Lose to Argentina and Ireland fall below France
beats: Ireland have been third in the world since July. They keep it only by avoiding defeat in Dublin: lose by any margin and France go above them. Argentina need a win by sixteen or more to pass Australia into seventh.

Ireland last played in July, a 21–40 loss in New Zealand that followed wins over Australia, 33–31, and Japan, 36–20. Argentina have won once in 2026, 35–21 against Wales, then lost three in a row before drawing 28–28 with Australia in September.
The Nations Championship table is tighter than the rankings: Ireland sixth on ten points, level with Scotland in fifth, Argentina a point behind Australia.

Andy Farrell names his squad on Wednesday without captain Caelan Doris, still sidelined, and with Jack Conan's shoulder needing further assessment after he went off against Clermont. Farrell's stated target is the title.
Both play again on 14 November, Ireland at home to Fiji and Argentina away in Italy. South Africa come to Dublin a week after that.

draft.headline: The leaders visit Turin; Italy are still on zero
beats: South Africa top the Nations Championship on points difference alone, level with New Zealand on 15 after three wins. Italy are 11th with no points, and their losses to Japan, New Zealand and Australia cost them 94 on the difference.

The rankings only move one way. An Italy win or a draw lifts them to 9th, above Japan, Fiji and Wales, and drops South Africa to 2nd behind New Zealand. A South African win by any margin changes nothing.
Italy have lost four straight, the last 10–57 in Australia in July. South Africa took the series off New Zealand, then made wholesale changes and lost 38–42 to Australia in Perth.

The sides last met on 15 November 2025, when Italy lost 14–32 at home. Victor Matfield expects Rassie Erasmus to test his depth this month, saying there are still "some combinations that we can get better".
Neither gets a rest. South Africa are in France six days later, and Italy host Argentina the day after that.

draft.headline: The Boks can only lose a place in Turin
beats: South Africa cannot climb in Turin, only fall. Beat Italy and they stay first. Lose, or draw, and New Zealand go above them. Italy, twelfth, would rise to ninth with any win, past Japan, Fiji and Wales.

The table says why that is unlikely. Italy are 11th with no points from three games and a points difference of minus 94. South Africa lead on plus 81. The last meeting, in Italy on 15 November 2025, finished 14–32.

Italy's July read 10–27 in Japan, 17–47 in New Zealand, 10–57 in Australia. South Africa also lost their last game, 38–42 in Perth in September, after wholesale changes to the side. Victor Matfield expects Rassie Erasmus to test depth again in November, and hopes he does not blood too many at once.
Dan du Preez looks unlikely to feature. Bath say the 31-year-old back-rower tore a hamstring in training: "That will rule him out for a considerable amount of time."
Six days later South Africa are in France. Italy host Argentina the day after that.

draft.headline: Scotland's route above England runs through the All Blacks
beats: A year ago, almost to the week, New Zealand won 25–17 at Murrayfield. Win this time and Scotland climb above England in the world rankings. Lose by 16 or more and they slip below Australia.

New Zealand arrive warm. They beat Australia 50–19 and 43–21 in October, after three straight defeats by South Africa. Scotland have not played since July, when they won 47–38 away to Argentina, lost 28–42 to South Africa and beat Fiji 33–17.

Damian McKenzie, 31, moved from full-back to fly-half for the Bledisloe Tests after injuries to Ruben Love and Richie Mo'unga. Justin Marshall's caution about the trip north: "It's a different scenario when you've got static ball, potentially go to the UK."

Josh Kerr, the mile world record-holder, delivers the match ball before a capacity 67,130. His boyhood picture of the day ended with "facing the haka before taking on the All Blacks. It doesn’t get much bigger than that."
A week later Scotland host Australia and New Zealand go to Wales.

draft.headline: A year on, Scotland get another shot at the All Blacks
beats: A year ago on this ground Scotland lost 17–25 to New Zealand. The All Blacks are back for Scotland's first Nations Championship home game, in front of a capacity 67,130 crowd, with world mile record-holder Josh Kerr delivering the match ball.
Win and Scotland go above England into fifth. Lose by sixteen or more and they drop below Australia, who visit Murrayfield the following week. New Zealand stay second either way.

New Zealand are three from three in the Championship and have won their last two, 50–19 and 43–21 against Australia, after three straight losses to South Africa. Scotland's last outing was a 33–17 win in Fiji in July.

Damian McKenzie, 31, started those two Bledisloe Tests at fly-half with Richie Mo'unga and Ruben Love injured. Justin Marshall rates the shift a success but expects static ball and an opposition "a bit more niggly at the breakdown" to make the UK leg harder.
New Zealand go to Wales a week later.

draft.headline: Japan arrive in Cardiff ranked above Wales
beats: Last November Wales beat Japan 24–23 in Cardiff. Since then Japan have won the Pacific Nations Cup, edging Fiji 20–15 in Tokyo in September, and climbed from 12th to 9th in the world. Wales have slipped to 11th.
Japan come in on three straight wins, the other two 63–14 against the USA and 57–12 against Canada. Wales lost their last two, both in July: 21–35 in Argentina and 0–43 in South Africa.
A Wales win takes them back up to 9th, above Japan. Whoever loses drops below Italy, who have yet to win in the Nations Championship.

Taulupe Faletau, 35 and 109 caps, won his last one against Japan in the summer of 2025. He misses this squad, though Steve Tandy says "we would definitely not rule anyone out". Uncapped Dragons backs Che Hope and Aneurin Owen are in.
A week later Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England.

draft.headline: Wales beat Japan by a point; now they look up at them
beats: Their last meeting, here on 15 November 2025, Wales won 24–23. Since then Japan have climbed to ninth in the world, helped by September's 20–15 Pacific Nations Cup win over Fiji in Tokyo. Wales sit eleventh.

Win and Wales go back above Japan and Fiji into ninth. Lose and they fall below Italy, twelfth at best. The Nations Championship table already has them a point apart, ninth and tenth, with Italy and Fiji below on nothing.
Form points the other way. Wales lost 21–35 in Argentina and 0–43 in South Africa, no tries in the second. Japan have won three straight: 57–12, 63–14, 20–15.

Steve Tandy's 39-man squad has uncapped Dragons backs Che Hope and Aneurin Owen. Taulupe Faletau, 35, 109 caps, is not in it; his last Test was against Japan in 2025. Tandy says "we would definitely not rule anyone out".
A week later Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England.

draft.headline: Jake White's first Fiji Test is France, in Lyon
beats: Fiji appointed Jake White, South Africa's 2007 World Cup-winning coach, on 13 October, less than a year out from the World Cup in Australia. His first Test in charge is away to the side fourth in the world. Former colleagues at Loftus Versfeld say his Fiji are "going to surprise people".

France arrive on two straight wins, 42–26 in Australia and 42–15 in Japan, with six tries in each. Fiji are bottom of the Nations Championship with no points from three games. One of those was 8–73 against England in July, and they lost their last game 15–20 to Japan.
A Fiji win lifts them above Japan into ninth. Win by 16 or more and France drop to sixth, below England and Scotland.
Their last meeting, on 15 November 2025, went 34–21 to France at home. Five days after this one, France host South Africa. Fiji go to Ireland.

draft.headline: Australia win and they take England's fifth place
beats: England have been fifth in the world since July. Beat them at Allianz Stadium and Australia take that spot, with England dropping to seventh, behind Scotland as well.

Australia beat South Africa 42–38 in September, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October. Victor Matfield, asked what they need to be a top-five side again, predicts they will not reach next year's World Cup semi-finals.

England have not played since July. They lost 45–21 in South Africa, then beat Fiji 73–8 and Argentina 31–24. Dan Cole worries the current style of Prem rugby could leave Steve Borthwick's side exposed in November.
Their last meeting, on 1 November 2025, was also at home for England. They won 25–7.
England host Japan five days later. Australia go to Scotland, the other side a win here would take them past.

draft.headline: Australia arrive on two heavy losses, fifth place on offer
beats: Australia come to London off 50–19 and 43–21 defeats to New Zealand, and slipped to seventh in the rankings this week. Win at Allianz Stadium, by any margin, and they go above England and Scotland to fifth. England would drop to seventh.
Victor Matfield has been setting out what the Wallabies need to become a top-five team again. One afternoon in London would do it, on paper at least.

England won the last meeting 25–7 at home on 1 November 2025. Their 2026 reads three wins from eight, though the last two were 73–8 over Fiji and 31–24 over Argentina in July. Dan Cole worries the Prem's style could leave Steve Borthwick's side exposed in November.

In the Nations Championship England are fourth, level on points with Scotland and Ireland and two behind France, with third playing fourth on finals weekend. Australia are seventh, two behind Ireland.
Next: England host Japan on 14 November; Australia go to Scotland the day after.
